audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings omit the post-closing GABX financing burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed first-half 2026 GABX amounts: $271.5 million revenue, $208.8 million expenses, $80.5 million interest expense, $23.9 million disposition gains, and $1.7 million net income; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings anchor excludes both GABX operating earnings and its post-closing interest, maintenance, integration, tax, and reinvestment burden while the bridge uses the post-closing balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: In anticipation of the closing of the transaction, on December 31, 2025, GATX contributed equity of $385.3 million to GABX, Brookfield contributed equity of $899.0 million to GABX, and GABX executed a $2.96 billion term loan to fund the acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The hybrid perimeter is demonstrated, not hypothetical. GABX generated large revenue and expense flows after closing, but its reported first-half net income was only $1.7 million and included $23.9 million of disposition gains. Because omitted operating benefits and financing and reinvestment costs pull value in opposite directions, the net direction cannot be established, but the scale is reasonably capable of changing the normalized owner-earnings base and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build a first-half 2026 GABX owner-earnings reconciliation, remove disposition gains, normalize interest, maintenance, taxes, integration costs, and maintenance capital, allocate the result to GATX common holders, annualize cautiously, and rerun all scenarios on one consistent post-closing perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Brookfield's 70% non-controlling claim can mismatch the common-share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed $68.4 million Brookfield share of GABX's $102.8 million cash at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.85 per diluted share and 1.6% of the $4.173 billion base equity value; excluding all $102.8 million would reduce value by $2.78 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated GABX cash or future earnings can enter the equity bridge or owner earnings at 100% even though the denominator represents only GATX common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the non-controlling interest represents Brookfield's 70 % ownership in GABX.
audit_findings.explanation: The current bridge demonstrably includes consolidated cash while GABX had $102.8 million of cash and Brookfield owned 66.5% after the June 2026 option exercise. The presently identifiable denominator mismatch is too small to change the conclusion: even excluding all GABX cash would lower the $113.00 base value to about $110.22, still far below the $178.11 price. This does not validate using 100% of future GABX owner earnings; that control remains necessary in a post-closing rerun.
audit_findings.action: Remove GABX cash from the common-share bridge unless its distributable amount is proven, and in every post-closing rerun deduct income attributable to NCI and include only GATX's economic share of GABX assets and cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The RRPF stake may be counted both in owner earnings and the valuation bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 RRPF after-tax affiliate earnings of $117.5 million and a $721.7 million stake bridge; if all $117.5 million remains in the $182.1 million anchor, the conditional computed base operating-PV overstatement is approximately $1.745 billion or $47.25 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: RRPF earnings may be capitalized through owner earnings while the $721.7 million RRPF investment is also added as a separate equity-bridge asset.
audit_findings.evidence: Our share of affiliates' earnings (after-tax) from the RRPF affiliates was $ 117.5 million in 2025, $ 82.8 million in 2024, and $ 72.8 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not demonstrated because the year-by-year owner-earnings reconciliation was not supplied. It is nevertheless an unresolved material possibility: the filed 2025 affiliate earnings equal 64.5% of the anchor, and retaining them while separately adding the stake could materially change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce every year's owner-earnings reconciliation and trace removal of RRPF earnings, dividends, taxes, and related adjustments. If look-through RRPF owner earnings are retained, remove the $721.7 million stake bridge and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: All reported cash may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum current exposure is the filed $747.1 million cash balance, equal to $20.23 per diluted share and 17.9% of the $4.173 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar even when some cash may fund operations, commitments, debt service, or VIE obligations and may not be distributable to GATX common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: We use these resources, along with available cash balances, to fulfill our debt, lease, and dividend obligations, to support our share repurchase programs, and to fund portfolio investments and capital additions.
audit_findings.explanation: The amount of required or confined cash is unresolved, although $102.8 million was held by GABX. Even the conservative upper-bound test of removing the entire $747.1 million would reduce base value from $113.00 to about $92.77 per share, still well below the $178.11 market price. The issue therefore cannot reverse the current valuation conclusion, though it can materially lower the reported value and buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by legal entity, restriction, ownership, near-term debt and purchase commitments, and minimum operating-liquidity requirements; rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrably distributable to GATX common holders.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized major maintenance may escape the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring major maintenance capitalized into operating assets may be omitted from the maintenance-capex deduction, overstating owner earnings and every projected DCF period.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize certain costs incurred in connection with planned major maintenance activities if those activities improve the asset or extend its useful life.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that qualifying planned major maintenance is capitalized, but the record does not show the amount or whether the owner-earnings calculation already deducts it. Because the valuation anchor is only $182.1 million, recurring capitalized maintenance could affect value, but available numbers cannot establish its magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain capital-expenditure rollforwards by asset class, identify capitalized repairs, compliance work, wheelsets, engine overhauls, and life-extension projects, reconcile them to each year's maintenance-capex deduction, and rerun if recurring amounts were omitted.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a nonrecurring insurance recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to the filed $17.5 million after-tax recovery; conditional computed base-value effect is approximately $259.9 million or $7.04 per share, reducing base value from $113.00 to about $105.96
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring affiliate insurance recovery may remain in the owner-earnings anchor and then be capitalized through the operating DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, financial results included $ 23.4 million ($ 17.5 million after-tax) of income from insurance recoveries related to aircraft spare engines.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the $182.1 million anchor is unresolved because its reconciliation was not supplied. Even assuming the entire $17.5 million after-tax recovery remains and is removed, the computed base value stays about $72.15 per share below the $178.11 market price, so it does not change the present valuation conclusion. Care is still required because $11.5 million related to a previously recorded impairment and must not be adjusted twice.
audit_findings.action: Tie the 2025 anchor to GAAP income and RRPF affiliate earnings, determine how much of the $17.5 million recovery remains, verify treatment of the prior impairment, and rerun after removing only the net nonrecurring amount not already purged.
